subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change direct Amazon Bedrock Nova generation models from forced no-cache to native cache-point eligible behavior once live Nova proof is attached?
rationale: Current main deliberately protects non-Anthropic Bedrock models with a no-cache wrapper, while the requested Nova support changes provider request shaping and user-visible cost/latency behavior.

options.title: Land after live Nova proof
options.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof showing accepted cachePoint payloads and cache usage, then land the linked PR or an equivalent narrow provider-owned fix.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in first
options.body: Preserve no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through explicit configuration or a narrower policy gate.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until maintainers have stronger live provider proof or a stronger AWS/provider contract signal.

recommendation.title: Land after live Nova proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof showing accepted cachePoint payloads and cache usage, then land the linked PR or an equivalent narrow provider-owned fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Bedrock prompt-cache runtime work makes this the best available routing candidate for the provider behavior decision.
